messages.content: San Antonio update: they added required certificate pickup after the closing panel, and Delta pushed my Sunday return later. Can you check whether keeping it is still the least-bad plan?

Yes. I will compare the retimed return against an earlier Sunday flight and a Monday return, then check the hotel note and seats. What time does the panel actually let out, and when can certificates be picked up?
Panel ends at 3:15. Certificate line opens at 3:30 and they said to allow up to 30 minutes. The retimed flight now gets me into Tampa close to midnight, which is ugly.

The trade-off is pretty clear. Keeping the retimed flight: SAT 5:55 p.m. via Atlanta, Tampa 11:48 p.m.; you can finish the panel, pick up the certificate, and still have airport buffer. Earlier Sunday option: 4:25 p.m. departure, Tampa about 10:10, but you would need to leave right as the panel ends and skip or gamble the certificate line. Monday: cleaner travel day, but it eats the prep block you wanted to protect.
So keeping Sunday is the practical answer unless they will email the certificate later?

I checked the conference note: they will email a transcript later, but the CE certificate for onsite attendance has to be picked up at the desk or requested afterward with a manual review. I would not bank on that if you need it quickly.
Agreed. Can we make the ground plan not ridiculous? I do not want to go back to the hotel after pickup.

Yes. Sunday plan would be: check out before the morning sessions, take your roller bag to convention bag check, attend the closing panel, pick up the certificate in the west foyer, retrieve the bag by 4:15, then use the Market Street rideshare zone. That should put you at SAT around 4:50-5:00 for the 5:55 flight.
Good. Also, did the suite confirm the room details? I heard the hot tub has service that weekend.

They confirmed the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and fitness room. Pool stays open. Caveat: the hot tub is closed Friday morning from 7 to noon for servicing; they expect it open after that, but a service overrun is possible. The connected block room still does not guarantee the mini-fridge, so I would not switch for this.
Keep the suite. Check seats on the retimed return and move me to windows if there are any.
Seat map is available. I can move SAT-ATL to 17A and ATL-TPA to 21F, both window seats, no fee. The outbound ATL-SAT leg still only has your aisle held; the window alert remains active.
Do that and update the rideshare notes around the certificate pickup.

Done. San Antonio stays on the retimed Sunday return instead of the earlier sprint or Monday travel. Return seats are now 17A and 21F. Sunday ground notes now use convention bag check, west-foyer certificate pickup, and the Market Street rideshare zone; no return trip to the hotel after the panel. Hotel remains the offsite queen suite, with the Friday-morning hot tub service caveat noted.

messages.content: I have a new Indianapolis request for an early-November seating and mobility lab. Friday and Saturday at a children's rehab practice. Can you build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, grouped by what will actually work?
I can. Which campus or landmark, and what is the earliest you can leave Tampa after the webinar?

It is near the Riley/IU Health area. My noon webinar should end at 12:45. I can leave for TPA right after that. I have to be onsite by 7:00 Friday. Saturday teardown may finish at 2:30, but could slide closer to 4:00.
Would you consider a Sunday return if Saturday gets too tight, or should I force a Saturday-night arrival home into the shortlist?
Show both. I would rather avoid the extra night, but not if it turns into a sprint with demo gear.

Flight shortlist by practicality: 1) Balanced: Thu 2:35 TPA-ATL-IND, arrive 7:18, about $340. You would need bags packed before the webinar and no errand buffer, but it works. 2) Simplest: Thu 6:05 nonstop to IND, arrive 8:30, about $520; costs more but removes connection risk and gives you a calmer departure from home. 3) Not worth leading with: later connection arriving after 11:00. Return: Sat 5:25 via ATL only works if teardown really ends by 2:30 and you can leave campus around 3:15; Sat 7:40 gets home after midnight; Sun 2:10 via ATL gets you home around 6:45 and is the least rushed.
What does the hotel side look like? I will have demo cushions and a small tool kit, so I do not want a messy morning.

Three logical buckets: Campus-adjacent hotel, about 5 minutes from the rehab site, around $185. It wins on proximity, but recent reviews are uneven, roughly 3.8-4.0, with AC and elevator complaints; queen bed and in-room fridge are not clearly guaranteed, and pool/hot tub details are unclear. Canal/IUPUI suite hotel, 12-18 minutes by rideshare, about $169-$189, rating 4.4; queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room are listed, but no hot tub. Downtown branded hotel, 10-15 minutes by rideshare, rating 4.2; coffee/fridge and fitness listed, no pool, and more event-night noise risk.
The adjacent one worries me. For a 7 a.m. start, is the suite commute actually a problem?

It is manageable if we build it deliberately. I would schedule rideshare pickup around 6:20-6:25, use the exact staff entrance instead of the main hospital doors, and have the host confirm where demo gear can be staged. The adjacent hotel saves minutes, but the room uncertainty is the bigger risk for an early teaching day.
Okay, put the suite hotel first. What do we need from the host before I decide on the return?

Ask them to confirm: whether Saturday has a true 2:30 hard stop or could run to 4:00; whether your demo equipment can be locked onsite if you return Sunday; exact staff entrance or rideshare pin for a 6:45 arrival Friday; load-in and elevator access; whether someone can help with teardown if aiming for a Saturday flight; and where luggage can sit Saturday after checkout.
Send that to the host. Keep the evening nonstop as a backup, but do not lead with it if the Thursday connection is sane. No booking until they answer.

Sent. Indianapolis working plan is: lead with the Thu 2:35 connection plus the Canal/IUPUI suite hotel, keep the 6:05 nonstop as the lower-risk but pricier outbound backup, and leave the return open between Saturday evening and Sunday afternoon until the host confirms wrap time and equipment storage. I also flagged the hotel caveats: the suite has no hot tub listed, while the campus-adjacent hotel has uneven reviews and unclear queen/fridge details.

messages.content: Indianapolis replies are in. They can end the lab by 2:30 and they can store my demo equipment if I come home Sunday. The hospital-adjacent hotel still cannot guarantee a queen or fridge. Can we book this now?

Yes. With those answers, the clean plan is the Canal/IUPUI suite hotel plus Sunday afternoon return. Caveats before you commit: the suite confirms queen, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room, but no hot tub; Sunday adds one hotel night. The Saturday evening flight is possible only if teardown is perfect and rideshare is quick.
I am set on the suite. Is Saturday evening still too tight if they really end at 2:30?

It is not impossible, but it is brittle. For the 5:25 departure you would need to leave campus by about 3:15. That leaves only 45 minutes for teardown, equipment handoff, changing, and any delay. Sunday removes that pressure and still gets you home early evening.
Then do Sunday. Book the practical Thursday connection, not the pricey nonstop. Window seats if you can.

Ready to book: Delta Thu 2:35 p.m. TPA-ATL-IND, arriving 7:18 p.m.; return Sun 2:10 p.m. IND-ATL-TPA, arriving 6:46 p.m. The suite hotel is Thursday through Sunday at the Canal/IUPUI property. Seat map has windows available on all four legs: 18A, 14F, 16A, and 21F. Shall I finalize?
Yes, finalize it. Add the notes about the 7 a.m. staff entrance and Sunday equipment storage.

Booked. Indianapolis is set with the Thursday Delta connection, Sunday afternoon return, and window seats on all four legs. Hotel is the Canal/IUPUI queen suite with coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room; no hot tub. Trip notes now include the 6:45-7:00 staff-entrance arrival, host equipment storage for Sunday return, and no need to rush to IND after Saturday teardown.
